name: develop_concept
description: Commit to one specific story direction for a short film inspired by the paper. Force creative choices — no hedging, no 'it could be...'. IMPORTANT: All array fields must contain plain strings — no markdown bullet prefixes ('- '), no embedded newlines (\n), no commas within a single item.

logline.description: One sentence. A specific subject doing or experiencing a specific thing, with stakes. Not a theme or a feeling — an event. Bad: 'A film about the loneliness of dying stars.' Good: 'A red dwarf star, the last light in a cooling universe, spends its final million years learning what it means to be alone.'

subject.description: The POV entity the film follows. Can be an animal, object, person, place, or anthropomorphized concept. Be specific — not 'a scientist' but 'a cartographer who has been mapping the same coastline for forty years as the sea takes it.' Not 'a cell' but 'a single T-cell that has been circulating in the bloodstream for eleven years without ever finding what it was trained to kill.'

central_image.description: The one frame someone would remember a week after seeing this film. Describe it in present tense as a visual: what is in the frame, where is the camera, what is happening. This image should contain the film's entire emotional argument.

structure.description: The invented narrative shape of this film, plus a justification for why this shape serves this particular idea. Do not use archetype names (witness arc, hero's journey). Describe the actual movement: what the film opens on, what the turn is, what the final image does. Then explain why THIS structure and not another. 2-4 sentences.

voice_mode.description: Wordless means no language at all — only image, sound, music. Default to this. Only choose narration, dialogue, or mixed if the specific phenomenon demands language to be accessed.

voice_rationale.description: Why this voice choice for this film. If wordless: what does silence do that language cannot? If language: what can only be accessed through words in this case, and why?

tone.description: The emotional register of this film, translated into filmmaking sensibility. Cite 1-2 specific reference films or filmmakers — not as templates to copy, but as shorthand for the kind of attention this film pays to its subject. Explain what quality you're borrowing, not what you're imitating. 2-3 sentences.

what_this_film_is_not.description: 2-3 obvious versions of this film that are NOT being made. Each item should name a specific, recognizable version and say exactly what's wrong with it: why it would be lesser, cheaper, or more generic than the film being proposed.

liberties_taken.description: What this concept invents, simplifies, anthropomorphizes, or otherwise departs from the science. Each item is one plain string: the liberty + why narrative needs it. No bullet prefixes. If you've taken no liberties, leave empty.

inviolable_truths_check.description: REQUIRED when the essence has inviolable_truths. One plain string per truth in the essence's inviolable_truths list — confirm this concept does not contradict it and note how the concept handles it. This list must have exactly as many items as the essence's inviolable_truths list. No bullet prefixes. No embedded newlines.
